topic: Smoking cessation in mental health inpatients
usual_baseline: Status is usually asked (66.7–92%, but 31% on older adult wards [3626]); treatment lags. NRT offered 20–25% [3558][3668]; dual NRT 0% [3427]; NRT within 30 minutes 0% [3626]; side-effect monitoring 0% [3558]. Detailed assessment under 10% [3181]. Cessation in discharge letters: one of 219 [3683], 3.3% [3558].
fix_that_works: Staff education and clerking reminders [3668]: status 66.7% to 93.3%, brief advice 33.3% to 84.6%, NRT 25% to 76.9%, referral 8.3% to 53.8%. A ward poster cut incorrect NRT prescribing from 22% to 0% [3124]. A standard smoking and vaping checklist gave full histories in both new admissions [3674].
fix_that_fails: A re-audit with no intervention fell from 71.88% to 36.84% assessed; after a shared presentation it reached only 57.14%, with under 40% assessed in detail, blamed on doctor rotation [3181].
consultant_advice: Many baselines; asking about smoking is mostly fine. The gaps are prompt and adequate NRT, dual NRT, vaping and plans at discharge. Audit time to first NRT, dose adequacy, and whether the discharge letter carries a cessation plan and medication adjustment [3683].
